head_commit.message:
BUG-0068 (secondary 2): normalize markdown-decorated Verify criteria before running

Wave docs may declare Verify criteria as prose bullets; the verifier ran
the raw section as one shell command and died with 'Illegal option -' —
W0 (14:26) and both W1 verification jobs failed this way, blocking the
campaign. normalize-declared-verify passes canonical declarations through
byte-for-byte; decorated ones get their code spans extracted and joined
with && (every declared command must be green). 29/29 verifier tests.

- tests: slow-lane seams, campaign integration, config wiring, IPC keys;
  exhaustion-path tests pin patience 0 for the legacy contract
- fixtures: go-orchestrator-baseline re-record (1497 -> 1589, target 1650)

runs.display_title: fix(release): purge restored workspace bytecode in the release test job (BUG-0065 root cause)

head_commit.message:
fix(release): purge restored workspace bytecode in the release test job (BUG-0065 root cause)

Root cause of the three identical release-lane failures (cohort-report
[ASSERTION_FAILURE] 122/5, verdicts collapsed to 'unverified'): the
release test job runs in the prepared-env RESTORE lane, which skips
setup-racket's stale-bytecode purge. Restored .zo snapshots carry mtimes
NEWER than the fresh checkout, so Racket executes the producer's
bytecode instead of the checked-out sources. Proven by the executed
suite name in the CI artifact: 'final-claim verdict cohort (c3,
v1.00.27 w5)' — lowercase — a W5-development-era source that does not
exist in the tagged tree (the tag's file reads uppercase '(C3, ... W5)').

- release.yml test job: purge all workspace .zo/compiled before the
  fast suite (preserving the frozen metadata-discovery fixture), so the
  lane tests exactly what it checked out
- test-ci-cohort-report.rkt: permanent BUG-0065 diagnostic dump — the
  fully-guarded gate state lands in per-file output on every run
- workflow-contract tests pin the purge step and the diagnostics

Local reproduction matched the mechanism exactly: editing the test
(recompile) over a stale module .zo reproduced the 5 failures;
purging fixed it (25/25).

runs.display_title: fix: dispatch symbol ev-keys to string-keyed TUI reducers (BUG-0062)

head_commit.message:
fix: dispatch symbol ev-keys to string-keyed TUI reducers (BUG-0062)

Live GSD emitters publish symbol event names (emit-gsd-event!
'gsd.verification.started) while the reducer registry is keyed by
strings — apply-event-to-state silently dropped every gsd.* event at
dispatch. This made the coordinator-owned verification lane invisible
despite BUG-0058's events/reducers being correct and fully tested:
tests construct string-ev events, matching the registry, while the
only live producer uses symbols.

- normalize symbol ev-keys to strings in apply-event-to-state; the
  fix restores the whole gsd.* event family live (verification
  started/completed/escalated, wave.outcome-error, plan.archived,
  campaign.infra-retry/notified)
- approved verification now leaves a durable transcript line with
  elapsed time and log path instead of clearing the status bar
  silently (truthful final state, BUG-0058 follow-through)
- regression tests construct the exact live shape (symbol ev +
  GSD-wrapped payload); previous string-shape tests kept unchanged

Fast suite: 1173/1173 files pass (isolated HOME).

runs.display_title: fix: surface coordinator-owned verification progress in the TUI (#9584)

head_commit.message:
fix: surface coordinator-owned verification progress in the TUI (#9584)

BUG-0058: a healthy multi-minute /go delivery gate previously left the
TUI showing the executor's final message with no verifying state,
inviting unnecessary interruption of a passing gate.

- delivery-verifier: registry-run-verify now emits typed progress
  events (best-effort, never affects verification semantics):
  * gsd.verification.started — wave, command, timeout budget, durable
    log path, attach flag, start time
  * gsd.verification.completed — state, exit code, verdict/reason
    (reducer-compatible), real elapsed seconds, log path; contents of
    the log are never emitted (bounded by contract)
- tui/state-types: new streaming-state verification-progress field
  (hash or #f) with ui-state-verification-progress + set-verification-
  progress accessors
- tui/state-events: started renders 'W<N> verifying — budget <t>s ·
  log <path>' and stores the start time; completed clears progress and
  enriches rejection entries with elapsed + log path; legacy
  artifact-count payloads render unchanged
- tui/render/status-line: live 'Xm Ys elapsed' suffix while the gate
  is active, computed from the stored start time
- tests: coordinator emission regression (started/completed payloads
  incl. verdict, exit code, elapsed, log path) + 6 TUI reducer/render
  regressions incl. acceptance-criteria sequence (verifying visible,
  cleared on approve)

Focused: delivery-verifier 24/24, TUI verification display 20/20,
render contracts + state-types green. Fast (isolated HOME):
1173/1173 files, 17177/17177 tests.

runs.display_title: fix: bounded same-wave verification repair with exact diagnostics (#9583)

head_commit.message:
fix: bounded same-wave verification repair with exact diagnostics (#9583)

BUG-0060: a repairable declared-Verify failure now gets one bounded
same-wave repair attempt instead of an immediate terminal wave failure.

- policy: new current-gsd-wave-verification-repair-retries (default 1,
  nonnegative-integer-guarded), independent of no-change/infra budgets
- verification-repair.rkt (new): repairable-rejection classification
  (owned verify cmd/exit/log evidence only), head-progress guard, and
  the durable retry transition (pending + persist + repair event +
  verification-repair-context-block with verbatim diagnostics)
- delivery-verifier: failing verify evidence now carries a bounded
  failed-output-summary (last 4 KiB) alongside cmd/exit/state/log so
  the repair executor sees coordinator-only diagnostics
- go-orchestrator: repair branch retains the same branch/worktree
  (call-with-retained-wave-worktree!), consumes a fresh fenced attempt,
  resets the wave to pending, and fails closed on exhaustion or an
  unchanged head (repair-exhausted event, truthful final state)
- wave-outcome-reporting.rkt (new): emit-wave-outcome-error! +
  runner-outcome-failure-reason extracted for BUG-0042 size discipline
  (go-orchestrator 1499 -> 1497 lines, 24 -> 22 defines; fixture
  re-recorded in the same commit)
- events: gsd.verification.repair-started / repair-exhausted
- tests: repair success, budget exhaustion, no-progress guard,
  cancellation during repair, bounded diagnostics, unit classification;
  inventory/count fixtures updated (params 228->229, modules 44->46)

Focused: 149/149 across 6 files + characterization 12/12.
Fast (isolated HOME): 1173/1173 files, 17176/17176 tests.

head_commit.message:
fix(tests): notifier desktop-command scratch needs tmp/ parent (CI-only failure)

test-campaign-notifier's desktop-command sink writes to
tmp/notify-desktop-test.out via `echo >>`. tmp/ is gitignored and
absent in fresh CI checkouts, so the shell exits 2 and the assertion
fails 9/1. Local runs masked it because the repo-local tmp/ exists.
Ensure the parent dir exists (make-directory* "tmp") before firing
the sink. Verified: 10/10 in a fresh worktree (previously 9/1),
matching the release-run failure exactly.

runs.display_title: fix(provider-retry): BUG-0022 — health gate no longer truncates same-turn retries to 2/5

head_commit.message:
fix(provider-retry): BUG-0022 — health gate no longer truncates same-turn retries to 2/5

The provider health gate (window 60s, threshold 3) recorded every retry
failure, so a fast-repeating error tripped the 3/60s threshold after
exactly 2 same-turn retries (min(max-retries, threshold-1)) — the
'[SYS] [retry: attempt 2/5]' → 'after 2 retries' truncation symptom.

Fix: only the turn-INITIAL failure (attempt 0) feeds the health window.
Same-turn retries stay bounded by max-retries, per-type budgets, the
cumulative ceiling, and the held/stall/silent-overflow breakers.
Cross-turn protection is preserved: a genuinely sick provider still
trips the gate on the next turn's initial failure.

Gate denials now surface visibly: provider.health-gate trace gains the
'attempt field, and a circuit-breaker retry event is emitted so the TUI
transcript explains the early stop (generic wording in tool-events).

Tests:
- new tests/test-bug-0022-health-gate-truncation.rkt (2/2): full 5-retry
  budget within a turn; cross-turn gate denial still works
- characterization pin flipped 2 -> 5 (test-gsd-executor-retry-*)
- model-switch e2e + session error correlation recalibrated to the
  full budget (fail-times 6 > 1+5)
- test-test-lint: subprocess-wait before reading exit status (flake fix)
- fast suite: 1141 pass, 0 fail (delivery-verifier 2m timeout is a
  pre-existing per-file-limit issue, passes solo in 2m15s)

runs.display_title: fix(gsd): BUG-0037 W2 — hook dropped tool arguments; all bash calls collapsed into one signature

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): BUG-0037 W2 — real root cause: hook dropped tool arguments, collapsing all bash calls into one signature

Fourth live false-kill exposed the actual defect. The watchdog never
saw arguments at all:

* step-executor.rkt built the post-tool-result hook messages with only
  'content and 'name. The stall signature (name + arguments hash) thus
  degenerated to "bash|" for EVERY bash call — each kill fired at
  exactly the hard limit with 'repeating bash', whatever the limit was
  (3, then 8, then 15). Threshold tuning was treating symptoms.
* wave-executor.rkt additionally truncated argument values at 64 chars,
  collapsing distinct long commands sharing the cd-prefix.

Fix:
* step-executor now carries 'arguments (from tool-call-arguments) in
  hook messages.
* Signature digest is full-fidelity: canonicalized ~s of the complete
  argument set; string-form arguments (provider JSON-parse fallback)
  hash by content; missing arguments keep the documented degenerate
  "" digest (defensive: identical-looking calls still steer/kill).
* New LIVE REGRESSION tests: 25 distinct commands sharing a cd-prefix
  never trip; 20 distinct string-form arguments never trip; missing-
  arguments repeats pin the defensive contract.

Fast suite 1141/1141 green.

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): BUG-0037 v3 — raise repetition limits to 8/15/30/300

Third live-campaign false-kill (v1.00.20 W2 attempt 3): hard-limit 8
tripped after only ~12 tool calls of legitimate exploration. The
executor was running different grep/find/git commands — not a true
livelock.

Raised all defaults substantially:
  soft  5 → 8
  hard  8 → 15
  window 20 → 30
  backstop 200 → 300

A genuine livelock repeats the IDENTICAL call dozens of times
back-to-back. Legitimate exploration spreads similar calls across
other work. The new limits give real livelocks (50+ identical repeats)
ample room to be caught while letting explorers work.

Auto-retry classification (PR #9536) confirmed working: the killed
attempt spawned a fresh session automatically. The thresholds were the
remaining issue.

Fast suite 1141/1141 green; pre-commit 18/18.

runs.display_title: fix(gsd): BUG-0037 follow-up — raise repetition limits; make stall deaths retryable

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): BUG-0037 follow-up — raise repetition limits; stall deaths classify as retryable

Live campaign evidence (v1.00.20 W2 attempt 1, killed 4 calls in):

* Thresholds: soft 2→5, hard 3→8, window 10→20. A true livelock repeats
  dozens of times; legitimate re-runs of the same grep/test between other
  work stay far below the kill line. Regression tests pin interleaved
  repetition (6 identical greps + reads + test runs) as never-killed.

* Retry classification: the executor session's tool loop converts the
  gsd-stall-exn into a loop-result 'error carrying the stall message, so
  the gsd-stall-exn? handlers at the runner boundary never fired and the
  death stopped the campaign. prompt-run-result->outcome now recognizes
  the canonical 'mutation-stall watchdog:' prefix and routes it to the
  retryable 'infra-failed path (bounded auto-resume with prior context).

Fast suite 1141/1141 green (second run; first run had an unrelated
load flake).

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): BUG-0037 W1 — repetition-based mutation-stall watchdog v2

Stall = repetition within a recent window, not mere absence of mutation.

* wave-executor: tool-call signature (name + normalized args hash);
  sliding window (10); soft steer at 2 identical, hard kill at 3;
  absolute backstop (200) for signature-cycling livelocks with INFO log
  at 75%; mutation resets counter AND clears the window; snapshot
  carries stall-reason/stall-tool/recent-tools.
* go-orchestrator: observe-hook records now carry 'arguments (without
  them every read collapsed to one signature); gsd-stall-exn maps to
  RETRYABLE 'infra-failed outcome at both conversion sites so watchdog
  deaths auto-resume with prior-attempt context instead of halting the
  campaign; hard-failure message names looped tool + recent tools.
* tests: characterization pins flipped to v2 regression suite; legacy
  watchdog suite rewritten to v2 semantics (70 distinct reads never
  trip; identical triple kills; backstop; inert opt-outs).

Fast suite 1141/1141 green. Fixes BUG-0037.

W1 core (BUG-0028): ipc-request gains coordinator-authoritative
trusted-working-dir; worker-dispatch extends request-scoped allowed-roots

runs.display_title: fix(gsd): worktree-isolation default OFF — worker allowed-roots stale across recreations (BUG-0028)

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): roll worktree-isolation default back to OFF (BUG-0028 hotfix)

With isolation ON, per-attempt worktrees invalidate the tool worker's
captured allowed-roots (current-allowed-roots = cwd at worker start,
never refreshed), so executors cannot edit any path — main checkout or
their own worktree — and fall back to raw shell mutation that bypasses
Racket-aware guards. Roll the default to OFF (proven legacy path) until
worker allowed-roots track worktree lifecycle; #:isolate? #t remains the
opt-in. Test expectations flipped accordingly.

head_commit.message:
W3: prepared-env fast-gate cutover (ubuntu) + FAST_SHARD_COUNT guarded study

Fast-gate fixed-overhead cut on two axes (v1.00.16 W3):

1. Prepared-environment cutover, ubuntu fast-gate lanes only
   - ci.yml: new fast-env producer job (prepare-racket-environment,
     24h immutable artifact prepared-env-fast; skipped on
     workflow_dispatch and by RACKET_PREPARED_ARTIFACT=off).
   - test shards need fast-env; PREPARED_ENV resolves 'auto' only when
     producer green + not dispatch + rollback switch not off; else 'off'.
   - setup-racket gains guarded prepared-environment input (default off,
     Linux-only, requires installer SHA): verified restore skips
     install+compile (restore's 4 read-only health checks replace them);
     any mismatch falls back to the full path flagged ::warning +
     REBUILT step summary — never silent. All other call sites unchanged.
   - CI-RACKET-CACHE-POLICY.md: explicit ubuntu-vs-macOS lane split;
     macOS platform lane keeps compile-on-every-hit (v1.00.10 condition).

2. FAST_SHARD_COUNT guarded shard study (FAST_SHARD_PLAN precedent)
   - New repo variable FAST_SHARD_COUNT, default 3 = [0,1,2]; matrix
     widens only on exact 4/6/8 values.
   - shard-plan-report runs report-only 4/6/8 predictions over post-W1/W2
     durations; activation rule + revert command recorded in
     test-regression-log.md (decision: KEEP 3 pending study artifact).

Gate structure, job names, required checks unchanged; selector-flag grep
in .github/workflows/ stays 0.

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): tolerate em-dash wave headers + 1-based plan numbering (v1.00.14 hotfix)

Session MN5MQHQP: a plan written as '## Wave 1 — Title' failed /go with
'Wave indices not sequential 0..3: (0 0 0 0)' — the parser only matched
the colon separator, silently defaulting every wave to index 0.

- plan-types-parser.rkt: header separator may now be ':', em/en-dash,
  or a hyphen run.
- plan-types.rkt parse-waves-from-markdown: an EXACT 1..n sequential run
  is normalized to the internal 0-based indexing; anything else is left
  untouched so normalize-plan still rejects genuinely broken numbering.

Regression test: tests/test-plan-wave-header-tolerance.rkt (reproduces
the exact failing plan shape).

runs.display_title: fix(BUG-0018): thinking-gap cap, /model request-path fix, retry economics (v1.00.14)

head_commit.message:
fix(BUG-0018): configurable thinking-gap cap, /model reaches request path, retry economics (v1.00.14)

W1: per-model timeouts.models.<model>.thinking-gap-cap widens the SSE
thinking-idle window past the legacy 300s bound (widen-only); ops-level
current-max-thinking-gap-secs parameter preserves v1.00.13 defaults.
Keepalive liveness documented + tested (heartbeat frames reset the idle clock).

W2: set-model!/switch-model! record an explicit 'model-override marker;
build-session-context-for-prompt E4 no longer clobbers it with the
path-derived model each prompt; dispatch-iteration reconciles divergence
loudly; handle-model-command refuses UI-only switches, guarantees a
model.switched event (logger fallback when bus nil), transcript only
after mutation success.

W3: silent-thinking overflows (thinking phase, zero chars) get exactly one
retry then circuit-break with guidance; overflow backoff scales with the
consumed window. GSD executor sessions inherit the coordinator's switched
provider/model via runtime/session/executor-inheritance.rkt.

Version 1.00.14.

runs.display_title: fix(pre-commit): staged fmt check fails loudly instead of rewriting

head_commit.message:
fix(pre-commit): staged fmt check fails loudly instead of rewriting (#9501)

run-staged-lint ran `raco fmt -i` during the hook: the index snapshot
kept the unformatted content while the working tree was silently
rewritten, dirtying the tree after the commit landed (observed during
the v1.00.13 release session).

check-fmt-canonical now diffs `raco fmt <file>` stdout against the
file (no rewrite; `raco fmt --check` does not exist) and the hook
fails with a re-stage hint. Regression tests: structural (no
execution of raco fmt -i remains) + behavioral (bad file detected and
left byte-identical; canonical file passes).

Co-authored-by: coinerd <coinerd@users.noreply.github.com>

suite — 0 of its tests reference it). Verified locally: git archive
with the attribute produces 0 links and 0 fixture entries.

head_commit.message:
fix(ci): workspace bytecode wipe spares frozen discovery fixture

The setup-racket action (and two ci.yml clear-stale-bytecode steps)
rm -rf every compiled/ directory in the workspace. The frozen
discovery-parity fixture keeps a TRACKED stray .rkt inside
tests/metadata-discovery/fixture/tests/compiled/ — the wipe deleted it
at job start, surfacing as exactly '1 uncommitted change' at the
release git-clean gate (named by the #9496 diagnostic after three
failing tag-publish runs). Exclude the fixture tree from the wipes;
it contains no bytecode by design.

runs.display_title: feat(liveness): v1.00.13 W4 — connect/TTFB bound, hard deadlines, heartbeat-aware liveness (#9478)

head_commit.message:
feat(liveness): v1.00.13 W4 — connect/TTFB bound, hard deadlines, heartbeat-aware liveness (#9478)

Every generic blocking phase is bounded by one resolved policy and every
retry-relevant liveness fact is structured (RL-4/RL-8/RL-9, NP-7):

- llm/http-helpers.rkt: provider-sendrecv/ttfb-bounded — connect+TLS+
  status+headers runs under the policy connect/TTFB window; an established-
  but-silent peer raises exn:fail:network:timeout:stream with structured
  phase 'connect/ttfb (never the full request budget); cleanup runs BEFORE
  the worker is killed. make-provider-http-request gains #:connect-timeout.
- all four adapters: streaming sendrecv and eager send paths pass the
  policy connect-ttfb value; the 900 s budget can no longer mask a silent
  connection on any path.
- llm/stream.rkt: per-read waits are capped at
  min(phase-idle, remaining-total-budget) — a blocking read can no longer
  overshoot the total wall-clock deadline by a full phase window (NP-7).

runs.display_title: feat(lifecycle): v1.00.13 W3 — headers, cleanup, structured failures (#9473)

head_commit.message:
feat(lifecycle): v1.00.13 W3 — headers, cleanup, structured failures (#9473)

The request boundary owns lifecycle metadata and resources (RL-5/RL-6/RL-7):

- llm/http-helpers.rkt:
  - build-network-failure-context: machine-readable failure context
    (kind/http-status/response-headers/retry-after-ms). Response headers
    are REDACTED to the retry-relevant subset (Retry-After, x-ratelimit-*)
    — authorization/cookie values never reach failure metadata or logs.
  - parse-retry-after-header: delta-seconds AND HTTP-date forms. The date
    parser is timezone-free (civil-calendar conversion — find-seconds is
    locale-dependent) with a deterministic clock seam (#:now-ms thunk);
    past dates clamp to 0.
  - make-provider-http-request now OWNS every response port it opens:
    idempotent single-owner close on success, status-check failure, read
    timeout, request timeout (cleanup passed to the request-timeout
    wrapper), and cancellation (dynamic-wind post-thunk). GC is only a
    safety net. Provider errors raised by status checkers are re-raised
    with the structured context attached (rendering still human-readable).
  - current-provider-http-sendrecv: injectable HTTP boundary for the
    cleanup-contract tests.
  - Duration contracts widened exact-positive-integer? -> positive? to
    match the downstream wrappers and allow sub-second test durations.
- llm/provider-errors.rkt: provider-error-context accessor (alias of the
  inherited q-error context field) — the boundary-named read for retry code.
- runtime/auto-retry.rkt: structured-retry-after-ms reads the structured
  context ONLY; with-auto-retry no longer feeds the exception message to
  parse-retry-after (RL-7: no string-as-protocol). parse-retry-after stays
  exported for compatibility.
- tests: network-failure-context + response-cleanup suites promoted green
  (6 + 6 checks incl. close-once matrix and 429/Retry-After fixture);
  heartbeat-aware held-request? contract split into
  tests/test-stream-liveness-classification.rkt (@not-test until W4 #9478).

Gates: 14 focused suites green (context, cleanup, http-helpers, auto-retry,
adaptive-retry, retry-telemetry, stream, openai, anthropic, azure, gemini,
policy, conformance, partial-result-preservation).

head_commit.message:
feat(adapters): v1.00.13 W2 — mandatory policy consumption across all adapters (#9466)

Adapters consume one resolved request-network-policy; they no longer
author generic timeout semantics (RL-3/RL-9/RL-10):

- llm/stream.rkt: current-request-mechanism-observer seam — stream-sse-events
  records (kind stream initial thinking content total) and
  make-provider-http-request records (kind body-read read-timeout) when the
  observer is set; the cross-adapter conformance harness observes the real
  mechanism boundary. Zero overhead when unset.
- openai-compatible: one policy per request; streaming consumes
  initial/thinking/content/total from policy; eager body-read consumes the
  policy body-read budget (legacy sse-read, e.g. deepseek 600 / kimi 300,
  replaces the flat 120 fallback — recorded parity fix). Local
  (max 600 ...) formula and resolver call removed.
- anthropic (+kimi eager): policy request budget for setup; policy kwargs for
  stream-sse-events; body-read from policy. Completes the v1.00.12 SS-6
  parity deferral: thinking window 60 -> policy value (min request,
  (min (or override 120) 300)); total 600 -> policy total (2x request,
  600 floor) when request > 300.
- azure-openai, gemini: same one-policy wiring for send + stream.
- tests: conformance harness promoted green (all four adapters, fixtures
  F1 deepseek-style request=900 sse-read=600 and F2 request=90); architecture
  test allowlist EMPTY (strict end state); observer parameter registered
  (SERVICE_HANDLE), inventory count 198.

Gates: 18 provider-focused suites, 567 tests green (policy, conformance,
arch, bounds, stream, model-timeouts, openai, anthropic, azure, gemini,
auto-retry, adaptive-retry, heartbeat, retry-telemetry, transport-arch,
differential-fixtures, change-locality, arch-parameters).

head_commit.message:
feat(policy): v1.00.13 W1 — semantic request-network policy module (#9461)

One pure owner for provider-request lifecycle policy (RL-1/RL-2/RL-9):

- llm/request-policy.rkt (new): request-network-policy struct
  (request-budget/connect-ttfb/initial-idle/thinking-idle/content-idle/
  stream-total/body-read), pure resolver with validation + safety caps,
  legacy sse-read compatibility mapping (feeds ONLY thinking-idle and
  body-read — never connect/initial/content), explicit-key precedence,
  model-driven resolve-request-network-policy-for-model, and the policy
  constants (single owner, AC-2). Total-stream formula frozen from the
  W0 ownership map: (max 600 (* 2 request)) — a total budget, not an
  inactivity detector.
- llm/stream.rkt: timeout parameters, constants, accessors, and the
  v1.00.12 sse-phase-timeout-secs resolver MOVED to the policy module;
  stream.rkt is mechanism-only and re-exports the compatibility surface.
  No behavior change (tests/test-sse-phase-timeout-bounds.rkt green).
- wiring/mode-helpers.rkt: wires timeouts.models.<m>.thinking-idle and
  .body-read into new parameters; non-fatal log-warning deprecation
  signal for legacy sse-read.
- tests: promote test-request-network-policy.rkt (green; adds
  model-driven resolution cases) and test-request-policy-architecture.rkt
  (green with the transitional W2 adapter allowlist documented inline).

Gates: policy+arch+bounds+stream+model-timeouts+openai+anthropic+
heartbeat+auto-retry suites 9/9 files, 407 tests green. Behavior-
preserving extraction (adapter wiring is W2). README metrics synced.

head_commit.message:
fix(ci): package-presence guard for cold user-package-store runners

The setup-racket and prepare-racket-environment actions guarded on the
exit status of `raco pkg show --scope user q`, but raco exits 0 and
prints "[none]" when the package is absent. On every cache-miss runner
(main pushes since e3983d4a, fresh PR branches) the cold path therefore
took the relink branch and failed: 'raco pkg update: package not
currently installed / package: q' (INSTALL_RC=1), skipping all required
checks. PR #9452 merged green only because its own branch runs had a
warm, branch-scoped actions/cache entry.

Fix: compare the trimmed pkg-show output against "[none]" (q_installed
helper) at all three guard sites — setup-racket cache-hit guard,
setup-racket cold-path branch, prepare-racket-environment cache-hit
guard.

Verified locally: absent q selects the install branch, present fmt
selects relink; scripts/lint-ci-readiness.rkt 0 errors; ci-package-setup
preflight green (842 modules). README source-lines metric synced (+7,
classify.rkt fixture exclusion).

head_commit.message:
fix(ci): restore action downloads the artifact outside the checkout (#9452)

upload-artifact stores a single directory's bare contents and
download-artifact (no path) extracted them INTO the checkout, leaving
addon-store/ and q-compiled/ inside the q package tree — the rollback
raco setup then compiled the duplicated package sources ('identifier
already required' for quickcheck). The old normalization mv also never
ran because its target already existed (the producer stages at the same
RUNNER_TEMP path in role=full jobs). Download to
$RUNNER_TEMP/prepared-env-download and locate manifest.json by search
instead of guessing the extractor layout.

runs.display_title: fix(tests): partial-result-preservation retry count is ceiling-bound (release-gate flake)

head_commit.message:
fix(tests): partial-result-preservation retry count is ceiling-bound (flaky)

The 'partial messages attached to exception chain' test asserts exactly 5
retry attempts, but the test passes an explicit 10s cumulative ceiling. The
ceiling is enforced on retry attempts (attempt > 0) in with-auto-retry; under
a slow/loaded CI runner the 5 synchronous retries (each carrying a 500ms
stream-timeout) can exceed the 10s ceiling, terminating the loop with fewer
attempts and failing the strict count assertion. This is the cause of the
release-gate failure (test job: 1106/1107) and the main CI 'test' job.

The test's own comment says it 'asserts the metadata survives, not a specific
count', so relax the assertion to >= 1 attempt (metadata survived partial
wrapping) instead of the exact 5.

fix(changelog): normalize v1.00.06 header to canonical form + required sections

The wave's CHANGELOG entry used the bracketed '## [1.00.06] - 2026-08-20'
header, but sync-readme-status's changelog-header-rx only matches the plain
'## vX.Y.Z' form. parse-changelog-top-entry therefore fell through to the
stale '## 1.00.05' header, making --check report 'README Status says
v1.00.05, q-version is v1.00.06' and breaking test-sync-readme-status.rkt
in the lint job (test shard 2/6).

Normalize the header to '## 1.00.06' and add the mandatory Breaking /
Migration / Operational sections so lint-release-notes passes.

runs.name: CI
runs.display_title: fix(gsd): delivery verifier recognizes merged-to-main wave delivery

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier recognizes merged-to-main wave delivery

When a wave's work is committed + merged to main (as the wave agent does when
executing waves step by step), the local HEAD equals origin/main and the
base-relative three-dot diff is empty — the verifier reported 'no wave target
files changed' even though the target files were changed during the campaign.
This is the same false-negative family as #9382/#9386/#9390/#9399.

Fix: thread the campaign's created-at epoch through make-delivery-verifier ->
run-delivery-verification -> check-wave-files-changed -> changed-files-set.
When created-at is known, also collect files changed in commits reachable
from HEAD since the campaign base commit (git rev-list -1 --before=<epoch>
HEAD), recognizing merged-to-main delivery as valid evidence.

Adds a regression test: without created-at the merged wave is rejected; with
created-at it is approved.

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier accepts git-root-relative wave file paths (#9384 infra)

Wave docs for v1.00.06 declare CI/workflow targets git-root-relative
(.github/workflows/full-regression.yml) instead of the canonical
repo-root-relative form (q/.github/...). wave-file->git-relative mapped the
repo-root form to '../.github/...' which escaped the git root and never
matched the changed-file set, so the verifier rejected the wave despite the
work being present.

Fix: when the repo-root mapping escapes the git root ("../..."), fall back
to the declared git-root-relative path verbatim. Accepts both conventions.
Adds a regression test with a true two-tier checkout (base-dir not a git
repo; git root at base/q).

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier must match directory wave targets

The v1.00.04 W5 wave declares a directory target in its Files list
("q/tests/memory/" — existing tests + new focused tests under that
dir). git diff --name-only lists individual files, never directories,
so check-wave-files-changed compared the directory path against exact
file paths and always reported "no wave target files changed" — a
false negative for directory-scoped wave targets.

wave-file-changed? now treats a wave target whose original form ends
in "/" as a directory target and matches it by prefix: ANY changed
file under the directory satisfies the target. Exact-path matching is
unchanged for concrete file targets.

Fixes the v1.00.04 W5 wave-failed (delivery verification) regression.
Tests: +2 directory-target cases (approve when a file under the dir
changed; reject when nothing under it changed).

runs.display_title: fix(gsd): strip wave-doc path annotations + retry-with-adaptation on wave-failed

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): strip wave-doc path annotations + retry-with-adaptation on wave-failed

Two defects caused v1.00.04 W3 to fail delivery verification despite
complete evidence, and left retries blind to the failure:

1. Wave-doc file-path annotations parsed into the path
   Wave docs annotate target files with explanatory prose in parens,
   e.g. "- File: q/docs/reports/test-regression-log.md (new:
   full-regression evidence log)". clean-file-path kept the parens in
   the parsed path, so gsd-wave-files held a path that never matches a
   real git file and delivery verification always reported "no wave
   target files changed". Now strips trailing " (...)" annotations
   (preserving real paths that contain parens without a leading space).

2. wave-failed retries had no adaptation context
   On delivery-verification failure the reason lived only in the
   campaign-result string; the follow-up run saw no reason and repeated
   the same mistake. try-complete-wave! now records the verifier message
   into the wave doc as a "## Last Failure" section (record-wave-failure!),
   and build-single-wave-prompt surfaces it as a "Previous Attempt
   Failed — Adapt" block so the next run addresses the failure.

Tests: +4 extract-last-failure unit tests, +5 clean-file-path / parser
annotation tests. GSD suite green (delivery-verifier 12, wave-completion
9, atomic-projection 7, campaign-state 24, go-orchestrator 39,
command-handlers-unit 31, plan-types).

runs.display_title: fix(gsd): delivery verifier must accept committed branch delivery

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier must accept committed branch delivery

Wave docs may instruct the wave agent to commit + push + open a PR
(e.g. v1.00.04 W0 impact-docs). The delivery verifier's
check-wave-files-changed only detected uncommitted working-tree
changes (git diff HEAD) and untracked files, so a wave that delivered
its work as commits on a feature branch failed verification with
'no wave target files changed' even though delivery evidence was
complete on GitHub.

Changed-files-set now also includes commits on the current branch
relative to its base (origin/main or main, three-dot diff), so both
delivery styles are recognized: uncommitted working-tree changes AND
committed feature-branch delivery.

Fixes the v1.00.04 W0 wave-failed (delivery verification) regression.

head_commit.message:
fix(test-impact): repair embed-impact-in-results! type bug causing silent-green CI failure

run-impact-selection! returns changed entries as plain path strings, but
embed-impact-in-results! unconditionally did (hash-ref c 'file), raising
a contract violation that the (with-handlers [exn:fail? (lambda (_) (void))])
swallowed — leaving impact-results.json WITHOUT its selection section.
The CI shadow guard (sel=0 AND esc=0 AND non_test>0) then correctly
failed the 'Step summary + shadow evidence record' step.

Fix (two parts):
- changed->path: accept both string entries (current) and hash entries
  with 'file (older callers), embedding changed_files as plain strings.
- Stop swallowing the handler silently: a failed evidence embed now
  prints the reason to stderr so it can never be a silent green again
  (W5 shadow-contract requirement).

Verified locally against the CI reproduction (merge-base b4ff6608 → head
20a5f27): selection now embeds with 23 escalations, escalated_broad=true,
68 changed_files — the guard condition is unsatisfiable.

runs.display_title: fix(llm): wire per-model sse-read config into SSE stream timeouts (wave-cancelled SSE stalls)

head_commit.message:
fix(llm): wire per-model sse-read config into SSE stream timeouts

Previously the config key timeouts.models.<model>.sse-read was dead:
wire-timeouts! only read 'request', and the SSE stream timeouts came
from hardcoded constants (thinking cap held-request-detect-secs=120,
content http-stream-timeout-default=60). glm-5.3 (default provider,
no config entry) fell back to the 120s cap — the exact cause of the
repeated 'HTTP read timeout (120 seconds)' wave-cancelled failures.

Now:
- stream.rkt: new current-model-sse-read-timeouts parameter +
  effective-sse-read-timeout-for (returns #f when no override)
- mode-helpers.rkt: wire-timeouts! populates the new parameter from
  timeouts.models.<model>.sse-read
- openai-compatible.rkt: openai-stream-request threads the model's
  sse-read timeout through; the thinking/initial cap and the
  content-phase per-chunk timeout use it, falling back to the
  v0.99.78 defaults (120/60) when the model has no override

Effect: glm-5.3 (config sse-read=300) now tolerates 300s per-chunk
gaps in both phases; deepseek-v4-flash keeps its tight 60s window.
Config change: ~/.q/config.json timeouts.models.glm-5.3 = {request:900, sse-read:300}

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): progress-aware consecutive-tool breaker + higher ceilings (BUG-0016)

(a) Make the consecutive-tool circuit breaker progress-aware: a turn that
    edits a NEW distinct file resets the streak, so bulk metadata migrations
    touching hundreds of files are never mistaken for a runaway loop.
    (agent/iteration/loop-state.rkt edited-paths field, counters.rkt).
(b) Stamp toolLoopLimit onto the final loop-result metadata so the wave
    outcome distinguishes a deliberate breaker-stop ("tool loop limit
    reached") from a genuinely dropped tool result ("tool calls remain
    pending"). (runtime/iteration/step-executor.rkt)
(c) Raise ceilings: current-max-consecutive-tool-calls default 30 -> 300
    (util/iteration/decision.rkt); GSD campaign override 200 -> 600
    (extensions/gsd/policy.rkt; go-orchestrator inherits the policy value).

Tests: +6 (distinct/same-file/multi-file edit resets, breaker metadata
propagation); iteration/gsd suites all pass. README metrics re-synced.

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier accepts issue-less campaigns + non-Racket waves

The /go delivery verifier falsely rejected two legitimate campaign shapes:

1. Issue-less campaigns (no per-wave GitHub issues) run on main/current
   branch, but check-branch-matches demanded feature/issue-N-wave derived
   from a STATE.md issue table. It now passes when no expected branch is
   derivable, and only honors STATE.md issue rows that reference the
   current plan's wave doc (stale rows from a previous campaign are
   ignored instead of being misread as issue mappings).

2. The compile gate ran 'raco make' on every changed wave file including
   ci.yml and .md docs, which fails on non-module files. It now filters to
   Racket sources only, and passes when no Racket targets changed
   (docs/CI-only wave) since the file-changed check already guarantees
   delivery evidence.

Root cause of the reported wave->coordinator->verification->next-wave
stall: W0's implementation+verification completed but the coordinator
marked the wave failed because the verifier rejected on both grounds.
Tests: +4 cases (issue-less main approval, stale STATE.md row ignored,
non-Racket compile gate). All 11 delivery-verifier tests + related GSD
suites pass.

runs.display_title: fix(gsd): wave-doc authoring prompt warns against quarantined gh-wave-finish

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): wave-doc authoring prompt warns against quarantined gh-wave-finish

The github-integration extension already implements gh-wave-start,
gh-wave-finish, and gh-board as q tools; gh-wave-finish is deliberately
quarantined (fails closed by security policy) because the external
authenticated PR workflow is the sole finalization authority. The wave-doc
authoring prompt gave no guidance, so planning agents could write
gh-wave-finish Action steps that can never succeed agent-side (the cause of
the W6 wave-failed status). Adds explicit FINALIZATION guidance to the Wave
Doc Format section + regression test.

runs.display_title: fix: edit-tool leading-whitespace auto-fallback + D3 consecutive-tool ceiling 100→200 (#9366)

head_commit.message:
fix: edit-tool leading-whitespace auto-fallback + D3 consecutive-tool ceiling 100→200 (#9366)

Root cause of the 2026-08-17 live W3 wave-failed (session
01M07A6YCFN12E8E0FYJFHT9FT): the executor edited a test file with old-text
whose leading whitespace was systematically +1 space per level (9/11/19 vs
the file's 8/10/18). The edit tool did exact whitespace matching, so all 6
edit attempts failed 'old-text not found'; the model kept recovering with
more tool calls (read/grep/edit) and the D3 consecutive-tool breaker fired at
100 after ~19 min / 101 iterations -> wave-failed.

Fixes:
1. edit-normalize: new strip-leading? option + leading-whitespace-normalization
   options; leading-ws-find-matches tolerates ONLY leading-whitespace drift
   (threshold 1.0 = byte-exact content after indent strip), returns unique
   spans, and expands the span back over whitespace to line start.
2. edit-contract: apply-edit-contract now auto-falls-back to the leading-ws
   match when exact fails (unique -> apply, multiple -> ambiguous, none ->
   not-found/fuzzy), so indentation-drift edits succeed instead of failing.
3. edit.rkt: success result surfaces 'Note: old-text matched after ignoring
   leading whitespace (indentation).' when the auto-fallback fired.
4. policy.rkt: current-gsd-max-consecutive-tool-calls 100 -> 200 so recovery
   loops that re-read/re-grep before retrying are not policy-killed.

Tests: edit-normalize (strip-leading normalization, coordinate mapping),
edit-matching-correctness (auto-fallback applies when unique / ambiguous /
not-found on content diff), edit-execution-parity (ws fallback succeeds with
Note, genuine content mismatch still fails with diagnostics), gsd-policy
(ceiling >= 200 <= 400). Smoke (308) + extensions (1511) suites green.

   'edit: <old-text>'. Prefer path/file keys in the TUI arg summary.

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): D8 — campaign-aware provider retry + infra-meta-fix without attempt consumption (#9357)

Campaign 81f9be4b W3 attempt-4: 30/30 tool calls completed, then ONE
transient 120 s SSE read timeout → progressive-stall circuit break →
turn error → wave-failed, attempt consumed. The executor inherited the
interactive provider-retry policy (max-retries 2, stall-breaker 2,
300 s ceiling) against a 1800 s wave budget.

(A) Campaign-aware retry scaling:
- runtime/provider-retry.rkt: current-provider-retry-max-retries /
  stall-max-consecutive / ceiling-secs parameters (defaults unchanged
  for interactive turns); call-with-provider-retry reads them.
- execute-campaign-request! parameterizes them to wave scale: 5 retries,
  4-stall tolerance, ceiling = min(900, wave-timeout/2).

(B) Infra-meta-fix without attempt consumption:
- infra-failure? classifier (go-orchestrator): classify-error domain
  network/provider, retry-exhausted marker, or stream/SSE/read-timeout
  messages → 'infra-failed outcome in prompt-run-result->outcome.
- wave-runner-port: 'infra-failed is now a valid terminal outcome kind.
- run-campaign-wave: infra-failed rolls back the begin-attempt!
  increment (status pending, attempt-count restored, current-attempt
  cleared), persists, and stops the campaign with a clear message so
  the user re-runs /go when the provider is healthy. Genuine
  agent/code failures still consume an attempt.

Tests: tests/test-gsd-d8-provider-retry-scaling.rkt (8) — parameter
defaults/adjustability, infra classification (provider/network/
retry-exhausted → infra-failed; contract/tool-loop-limit stay failed),
and run-campaign-wave attempt preservation semantics.

fix(gsd): D7 — get-base-dir context-type dispatch for planning-read/planning-write (#9356)

Campaign 81f9be4b W3 failed 5 attempts. D7 root cause: get-base-dir
(extensions/gsd/tool-handlers.rkt) called ctx-cwd — an extension-ctx
accessor contracted to extension-ctx? — on the tool scheduler's
exec-context struct. Interactive sessions masked the bug because
current-pinned-dir is set after /plan; campaign executors run
reset-all-gsd-state! (pinned-dir #f) so execution reached the broken
call and raised an instant contract violation, burning wave iterations.

Fix: dispatch on the actual context type — exec-context? →
exec-context-working-directory, extension-ctx? → ctx-cwd. Contract on
get-base-dir widened to accept both.

planning-write under real exec-context with pinned-dir #f (executor
condition), under extension-ctx, and base_dir precedence. RED confirmed
before fix (contract violation reproduced), GREEN after.

runs.display_title: fix: /go campaign reliability — dispatch watchdog, campaign-aware /retry, executor tool limit, lease owner (D1–D4)

head_commit.message:
fix(runtime,gsd,tui): /go campaign reliability — dispatch watchdog, campaign-aware /retry, executor tool limit, lease owner (D1-D4) (#9351)

D1: tool-dispatch watchdog in runtime/tool-coordinator.rkt — coordinator
phases run on a worker thread with a bounded pre-start deadline
(current-tool-dispatch-timeout-ms, default 60s). If execution never starts
(e.g. a synchronous bus subscriber stalls the first tool.execution.updated
publish — incident 01M05MCKP: 35 dispatches accepted, 34 started, turn open
92 min), emit tool.dispatch.timeout and answer every pending call with a
synthetic error tool-result so the turn recovers. Once started, per-tool
timeouts own the rest.

D2: /retry of a [gsd-planning] EXECUTE prompt now routes through the
extension /go pipeline via ext-command-dispatcher-box (populated in
tui-ctx->cmd-ctx) — full campaign continuation with attempt accounting,
fresh executor sessions, durable state updates, instead of the in-session
plain resubmit that wedged campaign 81f9be4b at the completion boundary.

D3: current-gsd-max-consecutive-tool-calls default 30 -> 100; attempt-3 of
incident W2 died at exactly 30 while the same wave completed with
24-consecutive bursts elsewhere.

D4: campaign lease now records owner session-id + pid (run-campaign! /
execute-campaign-request! / execute-campaign-token! gain #:lease-owner;
TUI, GUI, SDK call sites pass their orchestrating session id) — incident
lock file said owner "unknown".

Tests: tests/test-tool-dispatch-watchdog.rkt (3),
tests/tui/test-retry-campaign-routing.rkt (3), policy floor + lease
owner/pid cases; parameter-inventory entry for the new knob.

runs.display_title: fix/w7 changelog release notes

head_commit.message:
fix(tests): serialize test-test-lint (BUG-0014) + accept 1.x semver

Release CI (run 31918999901) failed at 471b86d7:

1. test-test-lint.rkt ran in the parallel batch (no @isolation
   subprocess / @mutates env tags), so its 'lint-tests.rkt runs'
   subprocess raced with parallel workers compiling test files;
   the lint scan hit a half-written file and crashed (exit 2)
   -> ASSERTION_FAILURE. Flaky in CI, passing standalone.
   classify-filters.rkt mutating-file? (F-7, v0.99.77) treats
   subprocess isolation as serializing; tagging the file moves
   it into the serial batch before any parallel worker starts.

2. test-self-hosting-deep.rkt Deep Test 9 hard-coded 0.x semver
   (>= 0.90); q crossed the 1.00 major line, so the version
   check regex would fail on 1.00.01. Accept 1.x line.

Also dedup the duplicated rationale comment block (botched edit).

runs.display_title: fix(tui): wrap [FAIL] tool-failure lines at terminal width (BUG-0002)

head_commit.message:
fix(tui): wrap [FAIL] tool-failure lines at terminal width (BUG-0002)

The tool-fail branch of format-entry built a single styled-line and
returned it directly, bypassing wrap-styled-line. Any failure payload
longer than the terminal width was hard-clipped by draw-styled-line!,
hiding exactly the diagnostic tail a user needs. Multi-line errors were
flattened to one unbreakable line first, making stack traces unreadable.

Route the constructed [FAIL] line through the same wrap-styled-line
algorithm the assistant path uses; continuation lines keep the red
style with no repeated prefix, matching the wrapped-assistant
convention. No wrap logic duplicated.

Adds 6 regression tests: 3x-width and narrow-width wrapping, prefix
preservation on the first line, full-payload preservation across
wraps, newline flattening, and short-message passthrough.

v1.00.00-PRE1 W2

runs.display_title: fix(tui): per-session scrollback path - BUG-0001

head_commit.message:
fix(tui): per-session scrollback path — stop leaking last session's buffer (BUG-0001)

create-tui-session derived scrollback-path from the global session-store
base, so <base>/scrollback.jsonl was shared by every session: each new
session loaded the previous session's transcript on startup, and resume
showed the wrong buffer.

- tui-init.rkt: derive scrollback-path from (agent-session-session-dir
  sess) (in scope at exactly that point); the per-session directory is
  created eagerly by make-agent-session and required by
  resume-agent-session. Also fix the stale create-tui-session contract
  (tui-ctx/agent-session/rt-config/scrollback-path, not the old
  path-string/integer/list/integer signature).
- scrollback.rkt: document the audited save/load lifecycle — load exactly
  once at startup before any buffer exists, save exactly once at exit
  into the session's own file; missing file at load returns '().
- tests: new regression test — session A writes scrollback, new session
  B starts empty (not A's content), resume of A restores A's buffer.

Fixes BUG-0001.

head_commit.message:
fix(tui): per-session scrollback path — stop leaking last session's buffer (BUG-0001)

create-tui-session derived scrollback-path from the global session-store
base, so <base>/scrollback.jsonl was shared by every session: each new
session loaded the previous session's transcript on startup, and resume
showed the wrong buffer.

- tui-init.rkt: derive scrollback-path from (agent-session-session-dir
  sess) (in scope at exactly that point); the per-session directory is
  created eagerly by make-agent-session and required by
  resume-agent-session. Also fix the stale create-tui-session contract
  (tui-ctx/agent-session/rt-config/scrollback-path, not the old
  path-string/integer/list/integer signature).
- scrollback.rkt: document the audited save/load lifecycle — load exactly
  once at startup before any buffer exists, save exactly once at exit
  into the session's own file; missing file at load returns '().
- tests: new regression test — session A writes scrollback, new session
  B starts empty (not A's content), resume of A restores A's buffer.

Fixes BUG-0001.
